Omarchy defaults guide

omarchy-settings-dev on Omarchy

Tomorrow's Omarchy defaults — skel files, fonts, and the Plymouth theme from the quattro tip — for testers only.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Install with omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings-dev (about 2 minutes; 1.7 MB download / 9.4 MB installed). It's the dev build of Omarchy's defaults package — /etc/skel content, fonts, Plymouth theme, helper scripts from the tip of the quattro branch. Not an app: nothing to open. Snapshot first and back up ~/.config — dev defaults can clobber custom keybindings and configs.

omarchy-settings-dev on Omarchy

omarchy-settings-dev is the development build of Omarchy’s own defaults package — tomorrow’s skel files, fonts, Plymouth boot theme, and helper scripts, straight from the tip of the quattro branch — for testers who want the next defaults before they ship in stable.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings-dev

Takes ~2 minutes. The store listing reports a 1.7 MB download / 9.4 MB installed. MIT-licensed open source, free forever, no paid tier, no account. Read the warnings below first — this is not a normal app install: it touches system defaults, and installing it on a machine you depend on is a bad idea.

Who should install this: Omarchy testers and contributors who want to run tomorrow’s defaults today and report what breaks. Who should NOT: everyone else. If you just want Omarchy to work, stay on the stable omarchy-settings package that ships with your install. There is no feature in the dev build worth risking your daily driver for.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. The mental model.

This is not an app — there is nothing to open, no window, no menu entry. omarchy-settings is the plumbing package that makes a fresh Omarchy desktop look and behave consistently: the files copied into every new user’s home directory (/etc/skel), the default font set, the Plymouth boot-splash theme, and small helper scripts the rest of the system relies on (per the stable package’s store listing). The -dev build is the same package built from the tip of the in-progress quattro branch instead of a stable release, so testers can run tomorrow’s defaults ahead of them landing in the main package (per the dev store listing). Installing it means your machine’s defaults start tracking unreleased development work.

2. Back up before you touch it.

This is the one step that matters. Omarchy’s update flow takes a Snapper snapshot before package changes (per the DeepWiki boot/snapshot docs), and the v4.5.0-rc2 release notes themselves warn to “make sure you have a working backup (or a snapshot you know how to roll back to) before you upgrade a machine you depend on” (release notes). Before installing:

omarchy snapshot          # take a snapshot you know how to roll back to
cp -r ~/.config ~/config-backup-$(date +%F)   # your customizations, in one place

Unverified on Omarchy: whether omarchy pkg add triggers the same pre-change snapshot that omarchy update does — confirm before relying on it.

3. Install it.

omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings-dev
pacman -Q omarchy-settings-dev   # confirm what's installed
pacman -Ql omarchy-settings-dev  # see exactly which files it owns

4. The three things everyone needs to know:

  • /etc/skel only seeds new users. The skel files in this package are copied into a home directory when a user account is created. On your existing account, installing the dev package does not rewrite your home directory wholesale — your live config comes from ~/.config, not from skel. What the dev build can change for you is everything else it owns: fonts, the Plymouth theme, and helper scripts in system paths. Which parts actually take effect on an existing install, and whether any migration runs for existing users, is unverified — check pacman -Ql output and diff your config before and after.
  • Upgrades can overwrite your customizations. Omarchy’s own upgrade history shows this is real, not theoretical: the Quattro (v4) upgrade replaced the shell, broke custom Waybar configs and keybinds, and swapped Alacritty for foot as the default terminal (daily.dev retrospective). The 4.5 release candidates keep moving things — shortcuts relocated, new default bindings added that can collide with bindings of your own (v4.5.0-rc2 notes). If you have customized anything the defaults package owns, keep your own copy (see the backup step) and expect to re-apply it.
  • The dev build is a moving target. It tracks the tip of the quattro branch, not a release. There is no changelog entry, no version announcement, and no “what changed” — the contents change with every commit. If something breaks after an update, the first question is always “what landed in quattro since yesterday,” and the answer is in the repo commit history.

5. Config location.

There is no single config file for this package — its contents are the defaults. The upstream sources live in the repo’s default/ directory (hypr, fonts, plymouth, sddm, limine, snapper, systemd, and more), installed to system paths including /etc/skel. Your own overrides live in ~/.config as usual — that is where your customizations should go, never by editing the package’s files directly (pacman will overwrite them on the next update, or leave .pacnew files behind for you to merge by hand).

Common issues & fixes

All items below come from the project repo, the v4.5.0-rc2 release notes, or documented upgrade walkthroughs — none are invented. The record for this specific -dev package is thin (it has no README, no issue tracker of its own, and no changelog); most items are documented consequences of tracking Omarchy’s development defaults. Anything not directly sourced is marked unverified.

After updating, my custom keybindings / configs stopped working or behave differently

Known pattern, documented repeatedly: Quattro replaced the shell and broke custom Waybar configs and keybinds (daily.dev), and the 4.5 RCs add new default bindings (Super + Q, Super + A, Super + M, Quake console, and more) that “could collide with bindings of your own” (v4.5.0-rc2 notes).

Fix: Check the release notes for moved shortcuts first, then diff your ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua against the new defaults and re-apply your overrides. Keep your configs in ~/.config, not in files the package owns. Unverified: whether the -dev package itself triggers a migration that rewrites user config, or only ships new defaults.

My default browser reset to Chromium after upgrading

Documented upstream bug in the Quattro upgrade path: “Fix the Quattro upgrade resetting the default browser to Chromium” (v4.5.0-rc2 notes).

Fix: Set your browser back with your normal default-browser setting (or xdg-settings set default-web-browser <your-browser>.desktop) after the upgrade. If it keeps resetting, check whether a newer dev build carries the fix — this one was fixed upstream, so a current tip-of-quattro build should not do it. Unverified on Omarchy: exact behavior of the -dev package here.

The boot menu flashes past / I can’t reach a snapshot to roll back

Documented 4.5 change: Limine now waits 1 second instead of about 6 and boots quietly, so most of the time you won’t see the menu at all (v4.5.0-rc2 notes).

Fix: Keep tapping any key (the down arrow works) while the machine starts and it’ll stop at the menu. To keep the menu up longer permanently, set your own timeout: in /boot/limine.conf (for example timeout: 5); updates leave a timeout you set alone.

Something in the dev defaults broke my desktop and I want out

Fix: Roll back first, debug second. Boot into the pre-install Snapper snapshot from the Limine menu (see the item above for reaching it), or restore the ~/config-backup-* copy you made before installing. Then switch back to the stable package — the exact command is unverified (confirm whether omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings cleanly replaces the -dev build or whether pacman reports a conflict). Report what broke on the project’s GitHub issues: the whole point of the dev package is that testers report breakage. Unverified: the exact stable-switchback command and whether customizations made under dev defaults survive it.

I installed it and nothing visibly changed

Fix: Probably expected. The dev package ships defaults, not an app: on an existing account, skel changes only affect new users, and font/theme/helper changes may only show up for new sessions, new users, or after a reboot (Plymouth changes need a reboot to be visible at all). Check pacman -Ql omarchy-settings-dev to see what it owns, and compare the installed files against the quattro branch default/ directory to see what you actually got. Unverified: which specific changes take effect without a reboot.

Pairs well with / If you hate this, try

Pairs well with

  • A Snapper snapshot workflow (omarchy snapshot before any dev-branch change, Limine boot-menu rollback when it breaks), a dotfiles repo or plain ~/.config backup (so re-applying your customizations after a defaults change is one command), and the RC channel (Update > Channel > RC in the Omarchy menu) if you want the matching pre-release Omarchy build alongside the dev defaults.

If you hate this, try

  • The stable omarchy-settings package — same plumbing, released and tested instead of tip-of-branch (omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings). That’s the right choice for any machine you depend on. If you only want one upcoming feature, wait for the next RC instead of living on the dev tip: Omarchy 4.5 reached rc3 on November 2, 2026, with stable still at 4.0.6 (techaeris).

Frequently asked questions

What is omarchy-settings-dev?

The development build of Omarchy’s defaults package. It ships user defaults, /etc/skel content, fonts, the Plymouth boot theme, and support helpers from the tip of the quattro branch, instead of from a stable release. It’s for testers and contributors, not daily-driver machines.

Is omarchy-settings-dev an app I can open?

No. It’s plumbing — there is no window, no menu entry, nothing to launch. It changes what a fresh Omarchy desktop looks and behaves like, and what new user accounts start with.

Is it free?

Yes. MIT-licensed open source, $0, no account, no paid tier.

Should I install it on my main machine?

No. The store listing itself says it’s for users tracking the development branch and “may be less tested than omarchy-settings.” Use a test machine, or at minimum a Snapper snapshot you know how to roll back to. Stable is 4.0.6; 4.5 is still a release candidate.

How do I go back to stable?

Roll back to your pre-install snapshot first. The exact package switch-back command is unverified — confirm whether omarchy pkg add omarchy-settings cleanly replaces the -dev build before relying on it.
